quotes.text: Stripe’s [Radar Plus](https://stripe.com/radar/fraud-teams) uses Radar’s AI models to estimate your chances of winning a dispute.

When a page limit applies, Stripe estimates the total number of pages in the final evidence PDF as part of an [API evidence update](https://docs.stripe.com/api/disputes/update.md). The estimate includes text and uploaded files already saved on the dispute, with your updates applied.

If the updated evidence exceeds the applicable limit, Stripe returns an HTTP `400` response with `error.type` set to `invalid_request_error` and `error.code` set to `dispute_evidence_page_limit_exceeded`. This check applies whether `submit` is `true` or `false`.
Don’t extract page limits or page counts from `error.message` for programmatic validation. The limit and page counts in this example are illustrative. The applicable limit can vary by dispute.
Keep the combined file size within 4.5 MB and the evidence within the applicable page limit for the dispute.

old_evidence.text: Stripe’s [Radar for Fraud Teams](https://stripe.com/radar/fraud-teams) uses Radar’s AI models to estimate your chances of winning a dispute.
The combined page count must be less than 50 pages

findings: The new page adds an operational API page-limit error contract at lines 95-115. On evidence update, Stripe estimates the final compiled PDF using previously saved text/files plus the proposed changes; if the applicable limit is exceeded, it returns HTTP 400, invalid_request_error, dispute_evidence_page_limit_exceeded whether submit=true or false. Handle error.code, use error.message only for human explanation, reduce evidence and retry; do not parse the example's 17-page limit or page breakdown as a fixed rule.

The May page separately stated less than 50 combined pages and a 19-page Mastercard limit (old lines 135-137, 182-188). November retains less than 50 in its formatting list (new lines 158-160), but replaces the later network-specific general note with 'applicable page limit for the dispute' (new lines 205-207). This does not prove Mastercard's old limit was abolished or that 50 pages will be accepted for every dispute; the source table and disputes concept currently present 19 as an unqualified current maximum and should be dated/qualified.

The named win-likelihood product changes from Radar for Fraud Teams (old line 35) to Radar Plus (new line 36) while the five-dot percentage table remains unchanged (old lines 43-51; new lines 44-52). This is a captured product-label change, not proof of account entitlement, model accuracy, or a new prediction feature.

Core evidence guidance remains: chronological and grouped presentation, relevant excerpts, authorization/delivery proof, file format PDF/JPEG/PNG and combined 4.5MB, one file per evidence type, partial-refund evidence, and Visa CE 3.0 guidance (old lines 14-235; new lines 15-254). The 12-point font and portrait layout remain recommendations rather than validation constraints (new lines 163-168); current source line 46 calls the font a minimum without that distinction.

The new error example at lines 103-115 includes 17 and 36 page counts only as illustrative message values. The current source's fixed limits cannot be used as the sole preflight logic; a page-limit error can occur even on an unsubmitted evidence update (new lines 97-101).
substantive_changes: New page-limit API error handling, including compiled-PDF page estimate, existing-plus-updated evidence scope, HTTP 400/type/code, submit-independent check and code-driven handling (new lines 95-115).

General limit note now directs readers to the dispute's applicable page limit rather than repeating the old 19-page Mastercard number (old lines 182-188; new lines 205-207); old number is historical, not affirmatively rescinded.
Win-likelihood product label changes from Radar for Fraud Teams to Radar Plus (old line 35; new line 36), without a change to the captured percentage table.
historical_claims_to_preserve: The May capture's 19-page Mastercard statement remains dated historical evidence (old line 188); omission from November does not establish repeal. Both captures say combined uploaded files cannot exceed 4.5MB and total formatting-list pages must be less than 50 (old lines 135-137; new lines 158-160).
The original one-file-per-evidence-type, relevant-excerpt, authorization/delivery, partial-refund and CE 3.0 guidance remains in November (old lines 65-235; new lines 66-254).
Win-likelihood 1-to-5-dot percentages remain 5%, 15%, 25%, 40%, 60% and are estimates conditional on relevant evidence, not outcome guarantees (old lines 43-51; new lines 44-52).
Stripe says it does not influence the bank's ultimate decision (old line 12; new line 13), and accepting a dispute still incurs a dispute fee (old lines 154-160; new lines 177-183).
conflicts: Current source lines 43-44 and disputes concept lines 97 and 324 present <50 and 19 Mastercard pages as static comprehensive limits. New lines 97-115 and 205-207 say the applicable limit can vary by dispute and an update may fail on compiled-PDF page estimation; retain old 19 only as dated evidence.
Current source line 15 names Radar for Fraud Teams; new line 36 names Radar Plus. Do not infer an account's Radar tier or feature eligibility from the rename.
Current source line 46 states 12pt as a hard minimum, whereas new lines 163-168 introduce it as a legibility recommendation, not an API validation limit.
unresolved_questions: The capture does not enumerate the per-dispute/network page limit or establish that the former 19-page Mastercard figure is still current or has been removed.
The HTTP error example's 17-page and 36-page counts are illustrative and cannot serve as global validation thresholds.
The Radar Plus label in the snapshot does not prove this account's enrollment or any particular dispute's prediction or outcome.

answers.Q1: At https://docs.stripe.com/disputes/best-practices, the November capture adds API page-limit handling absent from May: Stripe estimates the final evidence PDF and can return HTTP 400 with dispute_evidence_page_limit_exceeded on updates whether submit is true or false (new lines 95-115; old lines 85-94). [[source-stripe-disputes-best-practices]] needs this behavior, plus a dated note on the old Mastercard number. Radar's displayed name changes from Fraud Teams at old line 35 to Radar Plus at new line 36.
answers.Q2: For https://docs.stripe.com/disputes/best-practices, [[source-stripe-disputes-best-practices]] should retain the 4.5MB and less-than-50 formatting limits (old lines 135-137; new lines 158-160), but avoid treating May's 19-page Mastercard note at old line 188 as a verified universal current cutoff. November directs callers to the applicable limit per dispute (new lines 97-115, 205-207); use error.code for logic and treat the example's 17-page message as illustrative. Preserve evidence quality and bank-decision boundaries.
